gen_risks.description: Network capacity may be under‑utilised, reducing user fees and triggering reliance on the Revenue Support Agreement (RSA).
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure additional anchor or top‑up users early, include flexible capacity clauses and monitor utilisation to trigger alternative revenue sources.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 2.3.1 – risk of network underutilisation and revenue support exposure.

gen_risks.description: CO₂ leakage from storage sites could cause environmental harm and trigger compensation claims.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous site characterisation, continuous monitoring, and rely on the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA) for high‑impact, low‑probability events.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 1.3 – government will underwrite CO₂ leakage risks via the SCA.

gen_risks.description: Construction cost overruns on the T&S network could exceed the allowed revenue cap.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply cost‑sharing caps (40% recovery beyond allowance), enforce strict procurement controls and regular cost reporting to Ofgem.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.1.3 – T&SCo will only recoup 40% of any costs in excess of the agreed level.

gen_risks.description: Discontinuation of the EETH hydrogen plant or Protos ERF would reduce CO₂ volumes and revenue.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include performance milestones and termination penalties in contracts; maintain contingency users for the network.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 5.7.4 – Discontinuation risk for EETH and Protos.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient funds for de‑commissioning could leave a financial shortfall at end‑of‑life.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated de‑commissioning fund with regular contributions and escrow arrangements.

gen_risks.description: Cross‑chain risks between the T&SCo and capture projects may be poorly allocated, increasing overall project risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate specific risks to the party best able to manage them via the commercial agreements and maintain a cross‑chain risk register.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.1.2 – government largely underwriting cross‑chain risks.

gen_risks.description: Regulatory changes or licence revocation by Ofgem could disrupt network operation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain close liaison with Ofgem, comply with the CCS Network Code, and monitor regulatory developments.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.4.2 – Ofgem as economic regulator with licence powers.

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with the Subsidy Control Act could lead to legal challenges or loss of funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Submit subsidy assessments to the Subsidy Advice Unit early and embed compliance checks in contract design.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.2.5 – Subsidy controls and legal requirements.

gen_risks.description: Delays in delivering the T&S network could push back the Commercial Operating Date (COD) of anchor projects.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use phased delivery, buffer periods, and QSRA/PERT schedule assurance to monitor critical path activities.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 6.4.1 – overarching schedule risk to ensure timely COD.

gen_risks.description: Supply‑chain capacity constraints may cause construction delays and cost inflation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Early engagement with key suppliers, secure long‑term contracts, and maintain contingency stock for critical materials.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.1.4 – cost escalation driven by supply‑chain cost increases.

gen_risks.description: Current low UK ETS carbon price makes capture uneconomic without subsidies, risking project viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide long‑term revenue support via RSA and CfD‑type contracts to bridge the price gap.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 1.1 – costs of capture higher than emitting due to low carbon price.

gen_risks.description: Potential fraud in subsidy payments could lead to financial loss and reputational damage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement robust financial controls, regular audits, and fraud detection systems for all grant and subsidy flows.

gen_risks.description: Changes in government policy or funding envelope (NFE) could reduce available subsidies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year legislative commitments and embed flexibility in contracts to adjust to funding variations.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 5.2 – NFE of up to £20bn and reliance on exchequer funding.

gen_risks.description: Dense‑phase upgrade (Phase 2) may encounter technical challenges and higher than expected costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct detailed engineering studies, allocate contingency budget, and schedule upgrade after anchor COD to spread risk.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 2.3.2 – dense phase upgrades included in Phase 2.

gen_risks.description: Geological uncertainty could limit storage capacity or increase leakage risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform comprehensive site characterisation, modelling, and continuous monitoring of injection wells.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 1.1 – CO₂ stored in deep geological formations such as depleted fields or saline aquifers.

gen_risks.description: Long‑term RSA and SCA contracts may become unaffordable if cost assumptions change.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include periodic review clauses, cost‑cap mechanisms, and shared‑risk provisions in the agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.1.3 – RSA and SCA are 25‑year contracts providing revenue stability.

gen_risks.description: If build‑out projects fail to take FID, the T&S network could become a stranded asset.
gen_risks.mitigation: Tie network construction to firm user commitments, use the ‘uncertain cost reopener’ to limit CapEx exposure.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.2.2 – risk of network under‑utilisation if build‑out projects do not take FID.

gen_risks.description: RAB model cost reopeners may lead to higher than forecasted payments to the T&SCo.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous cost monitoring, apply the 40% cost‑sharing rule, and conduct regular regulator reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 5.1 – RAB model with cost reopeners settled ex post.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate data management could impair performance monitoring and decision‑making.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a comprehensive data‑management strategy, define data flows, and assign clear ownership for data quality.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 6.6 – data and information flows and data‑management strategy.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that government (HMG) is exposed to increased costs for Track-1 post-Financial Investment Decision (FID), and that cost pressures are unaffordable within delegated budgets. [Strategic Case risk T1SR1, Section 2.5 'Identify high level potential risks', p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Contractual mechanisms ensure HMG only takes on specific risks where appropriate, with liability limited and counterparties incentivised to control costs; governance mechanisms monitor costs and provide early warning of overruns; contingent liability exposure is accurately monitored.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the programme does not realise its intended benefits for Track-1. [Strategic Case risk T1SR3, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Projects undergo detailed technical assurance and financial due diligence; projects must meet Initial Conditions Precedent (ICPs) before contracts take effect and Operational CPs thereafter, with LCCC able to terminate and avoid paying for an underperforming project; contractual mechanisms allocate performance-related risk to the private sector; continued engagement with the global Carbon Management Challenge to expand CCUS use and deliver UK trade benefits.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the post-FID operating model across public and private sector parties will not operate successfully. [Strategic Case risk T1SR4, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: Medium/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Progress of arm's-length bodies' (ALBs') capacity (funding, resource) and capability (knowledge, skills) to operate successfully post-FID is monitored through the Delivery Board; a DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function will be set up between FID and Commercial Operations Date (COD) to mitigate risks to cluster delivery and system integration; readiness-testing mechanisms are in place ahead of FID; FY24/25 funding for the ALBs to fulfil their roles has been secured.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk of an unclear exit path for HMG from its role in the Track-1 commercial framework. [Strategic Case risk T1SR5, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Key planned developments include amendments to the process for granting economic licences, a move toward a competitive allocation process for capture contracts, and evolution of transport & storage business models to reflect an increased private-sector role in managing cross-chain risks; cost-reduction levers (UK ETS pricing, CBAMs) are intended to help cultivate a self-sustaining industry and enable an HMG exit path.
